key_insight: Visual Attribution Distillation (VAD) focuses distillation on corrections that are actually supported by visual evidence, rather than blindly copying all teacher-token corrections. This makes multimodal on-policy distillation more faithful and less contaminated by language priors or teacher-specific noise.
problem_solved: Standard multimodal on-policy distillation mixes together visual signals, linguistic priors, and teacher quirks in its next-token corrections. The paper addresses the challenge of identifying which student corrections truly come from the image, so distillation targets the right evidence instead of just the strongest signals.
method: Uses counterfactual target reconstruction to estimate whether a token correction is supported by visual evidence.
Separates visually grounded corrections from source-mixed teacher signals before applying distillation.
Reweights supervision so the student learns more from evidence-backed visual targets and less from non-visual artifacts.
impact: For practitioners, VAD can improve the quality of multimodal student models by making distillation more precise and interpretable. This is especially useful when training systems that must learn from teacher guidance without absorbing spurious language-only patterns.

paper_title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Kangning Zhang, Yixing Li, Shuai Shao, Qingyao Li, Zhengxi Lu
